utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This afternoon the schedule that we hear witnesses by videolink, but for the first witness to be called still an application for protective measures is pending, an application which is opposed by Defence counsel. Therefore, before we establish the videolink we turn into private session. Yes, Mr. Emmerson. One second, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Registrar. When we just were in private session, Mr. Emmerson, although not adding any reasons for his concerns, expressed the deep concerns of the Haradinaj Defence for the next witness to give evidence in -- through videolink. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I rise only to say that we are in a similar position and join in the concern that was expressed by Mr. Emmerson on behalf of Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With -- once again, with -- on the same state of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, you can of course safely assume that I join my colleagues in that concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said before, there's still an application pending for protective measures. We'll now turn into private session again in order to establish the videolink with the place where the witnesses are present, and we'll start with the witness ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber will deliberate on the application for protective measures and does not expect that it will take very long. We stand adjourned and parties are invited to remain in the courtroom. --- Break taken at 2.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio -- perhaps I first explain that he'll be examined. You'll now be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Please listen well to his questions and answer them. Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, I wanted to ask you some questions about your personal background, in early 1998, in the spring of 1998, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long had your family been living in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a long time. My great-grandfathers, my grandfathers lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you have a house in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was a new house just built.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When was it built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started building it in 1982. From 1982 to the moment I left, I spent money on building that house. I only worked to build that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And the land that the house was located on, whose land was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father bought that land, it was my father's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know of a family, the Haradinaj family or Haradinaj family in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know them. They are neighbours. My house is on the land of Ramush's uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's that person's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when did I buy the land?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, the name of the uncle. Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His name is Azem Iziri Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, it may be clear to you that ownership of the land creates more confusion at this moment than --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not going to go into it chapter and verse, I'm more interested in the geography of the structures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How far was your house from the Haradinaj house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the house of Ramush's uncle, from whom I bought the land, or Ramush's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm interested in Ramush's house, that's the house I'm interested in. How far was your house from the house that you call Ramush's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ramush's house was in the middle of the village about 200 or 300 metres from my house, and then they moved a little lower. It's not too far away from where I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Think back -- think back to early 1998, spring of 1998. You said that they moved a little lower. Now, in spring of 1998 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- in the early months of 1998, how far was your house from Ramush's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot explain exactly how far it is. Formerly his house was in the middle of the village, and later they moved to a place which is closer to Dubrave. Well, I cannot tell you how many metres, it's not kilometres though, it's metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Earlier you said that Ramush's house was in the middle of the village 2 to 300 metres away from your house. When you said that, were you talking about the distance that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that the distance in spring of 1998 from your house to his house, about 2 to 300 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm sure it was. I'm not sure which year he moved to that other house, though. Ramush, his father --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went and worked for Ramush and his father. We had good relations. We had no frictions amongst each other. They helped me, I helped them, together with my sons. We did not have any conflict with each other until the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the 2 and 300 metres were clearly related in the answer of the witness to the house in the middle of the village. So now we move again to 2 to 300 metres to the new house where he moved, where the witness said he doesn't know exactly when they moved into that house. That is all rather unclear to me. And there's another matter. I do not know where the witness lived at the time. If the parties would know, I mean such distances could be, I would say, easily agreed upon or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, they may well be. I've had no overtures from the Defence. I didn't think that this was the sort of issue that I should approach the Defence on to seek agreement on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the statement, I take it that distances from where you can see certain matters might not be without any relevance. So therefore the Chamber would like to have a clear view here. I don't know whether there are any pictures, I don't know whether we could ask the witness to identify where his house was at the time. And then of course the Chamber heard other evidence about where the villages -- about where the Haradinaj house in relation to the villages, but we need some --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I indicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would certainly be in a position to identify where we understand this witness's family home was built, but I would be most reluctant for that to be a substitution for the Trial Chamber hearing for itself what this witness has to say about matters of this kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because they go directly to [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that there are specific reasons why -- or rather not to agree upon these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll try and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, let's try to get as clear as possible where the house was located, where the witness and his family lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You said that the Haradinaj family lived in the -- in the middle of the village and then they moved. Okay. Now, of the two houses, the one that was in the middle of the village and the other one that they moved, which one was closer to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ramush's uncle's house was closer to me, about 50 metres away from me. Ramush was a little further down. I can't give you the exact number of metres. He was closer to the centre of the village, middle of the village. I don't know what to say. Well, I would describe it as being close to the middle -- to the centre of the village, and there are houses where they moved later towards Dubrave, closer to Dubrave. His uncles are there, and Ramush's house is about a hundred metres from there. Well, as I said, I cannot give you an exact number of metres how far it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's just forget about Ramush's uncles, let's forget about everyone except for Ramush, okay, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj. Let's focus on him. Just think about him. Just think about his house and where he lived, that's all, not his uncles or his relations, but just about Ramush Haradinaj. In the spring of 1998 where was he living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. In 1998 Ramush lived further down. He had left that house at the centre of the village, went further down between Dubrave and Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's where Dubrave ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I intend to move on from this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to know where the witness lived, I mean, so we can verify distances. Witness, could you tell us were you at that time living in the village of Gllogjan or were you living outside the village of Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was living in Gllogjan. I never left Gllogjan. Just when the war started I left of my own will. I had to leave to go to Gjakove because my wife was in hospital, while my family remained in the village. As I said, I never left the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to know, were you living in the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Myself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't live in the centre of the village. I'm further away from the centre of the village. It's not too far away. It's the road that leads to Shaptej, from the centre of Gllogjan, the road goes towards Shaptej. Shaptej is only ten minutes away on foot. From the centre of Gllogjan to my house is about 200 metres. That's all the distance between me and the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you, if you arrive in the village from the direction of Irzniq, yes, can you follow me? And if you want --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you want to go to Dubrava, is it true that then in the centre of the village you have to turn to the right? So from Irzniq --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. You have to take a right in order to go to Dubrave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in order to go to your house, do you also take that same road to the right in the village or do you take a different road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, on the left. You have to turn left. From the centre you turn left. It's very close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have a clear aerial -- and then from where you turn to the left, how far is it then, how many minutes' walk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes, not even that. It's very close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's a fair chance that one of the aerial views, we have pictures of aerial views, would show approximately where the house of the witness was, Mr. Di Fazio. Because I do understand that this -- at quite a distance from the house, we learned later to be Mr. Haradinaj's house or at that time to be Mr. Haradinaj's house. But I leave it in your hands at this moment. Please proceed, but the Chamber would prefer not to be left in confusion in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll see if we can make arrangements for the aerial map to be provided --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily, we have also pictures of -- aerial pictures showing houses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may draw your attention to number U0143045. I could not exclude for the possibility -- I don't know whether it's an exhibit or not, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll ask to see if we can get that up on the screen. Perhaps if I just proceed in the meantime and we can return to the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions, Mr. Jollaj, about your knowledge of Haradinaj family. You've mentioned Mr. Haradinaj's name. Can you tell us how long you had known him or you knew him back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To speak the truth, in 1998 I could not see Ramush very often. I saw him before the KLA came out in uniforms. That's when I saw him. I heard that he had come to my house, but I was not interested in very much in what the KLA was doing. I know that he was involved with the KLA and was wearing uniforms. I saw him on the street, passing. I was minding my own business. I was not interested in what he was doing. He had his own business, I had my own business. I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know him as a child, when he was a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Since he was very little, he was a toddler, because my son and Ramush grew up together. We knew each other. Both our families knew each other, uncles and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And his father, do you know his father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know his father. I've sat with him. We had food together. We drank together .

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thanks --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and we worked in the agricultural cooperative together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1998, was -- as far as -- if you know this, please tell us, did Ramush live in the same house as his father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to speak the truth, I don't know. I'm not sure, and I cannot tell you things that I don't know about. Please, don't ask me questions about things I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown D35, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to have a look at this particular photograph that's going to be shown to you on the screen that I hope you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, that can't -- I'm told that that's not technically possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, we can try and get a hard copy sent down on the break. Apparently there's no screen that's going to enable me to put this photograph to the witness. So I'll move on and I'll see if I can make arrangements for it to be sent during the break or sent via our staff outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this cannot be shown on the screen what we have now in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, the understanding is -- my understanding is that it cannot be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you, Witness -- did you know a gentleman, a Serbian gentleman named Otovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Otovic, I knew him well. I worked with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Otovic was a police officer. He worked in the police station in Decan. From Decan they came to Irzniq and worked in Irzniq. I know him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is -- was he killed in 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was killed, Otovic was killed in front of Ramush's gate --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just slow down. I'm going to ask you about him later, but not at the moment. Can you remember the date on which he was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. To be honest, I cannot remember the date. I was not paying attention --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- to dates and stuff like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. The answer's no. Do you remember the season?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to think about the period of time for about two months before he was killed. In that time, were you living in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In that time did you -- did you have an opportunity to see traffic coming into and out of the village at night-time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about nights. I was working non-stop, but I had heard from young people that those things were happening, that the Serbs, the police in uniforms came and ill-treated people. That did not happen to me. There were cases that I heard that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that they had police uniforms and they stopped people and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, just slow down --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and that never happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Slow down. Slow down. The shorter the answer that you give, the easier it will be for you and the easier it will be for me. Now, just think back. I'm asking -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It will be easier. Just think back in the period of time the two months before this fellow Otovic was killed. What I want to know is this: Did you during those two month or that period of time, did you have a chance to see cars or traffic moving in and out of the village, if that occurred, during the night-time, at night, cars and traffic coming in, people coming into the village in cars and vehicles? Did you have a chance to see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think the question -- excuse me, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think the question is as presently constituted as --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, would you please wait a second before you answer the question. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think the question as presently constituted as vague, "Did he have a chance." He's already indicated that he did not see any such traffic by virtue of a previous answer. I don't know whether at this point what Mr. Di Fazio is asking for is a possibility that something could have occurred or something more definite. And my real concern is the question as presently put together as vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't think so there's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That more or less resolves the matter. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps I should stop objecting regard to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I would not encourage parties to do so for this reason Mr. Guy-Smith. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I first address the witness. Witness, could you please listen carefully to the questions and try to answer them briefly, focusing on what specifically the question is about. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, look, you've told us, sir, that you knew about this fellow called Otovic and that he was killed. Did you see that? Did you see him being killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was close. I was passing on the road. I was coming from Gjakove. I stopped and I left. I went down to the stream because I was afraid that I would be killed myself --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay -- okay --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to get you to tell the story, but I'm going to get you to tell the story in answer to my questions. Okay. So we'll tell your story, and you'll describe it, what you saw, but only in answer to my questions. So you just listen to the question and in that way we'll start to explain to the Judges what you saw and what you know about this. Okay. First of all, on the day that he was killed, was it in the morning or in midday or in the afternoon that you saw Otovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was about 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning. I'm not very sure because I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you. You've answered the question. Now I'll ask my next question. Was he alone or with other police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was with another colleague. There was Mar Milic with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't think I got the name. Can you just repeat the name again, please, the name of his colleague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Momo Milic, he's from Palabardh.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So was Mr. Otovic just with Momo Milic or were there other police officers? Were there just two police officers or more than two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two, I saw two. I don't know anything about others because I left that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there a police car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And -- thank you. Now, when you saw Otovic and these policemen -- and his partner and the police car, what were you doing? Where were you planning on going or what were you planning on doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I heard the shots, I left that place and didn't go home until the next day at about 6.00, 7.00 in the morning. I was too scared to go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's just go back now and we'll try and get a bit more detail so we have the story in full. Okay. How far away were you -- when you heard the shots, how far away were you from Mr. Otovic would you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't be very accurate, of course, I was very close to Ljubica's house when I heard the shots, and you could see the police car down there on the road. Then, as I said, I was -- I became scared when I heard the shots, and I crossed over a fence and went to a meadow. And then after a while I saw many people gathered leaving the place going to Gjakove --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Can I ask you this: When you heard the shots, did you see who fired the shots? Did you see who fired the shots when you heard them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Hilmi, Ramush's father, whom the policeman asked something -- actually, I didn't hear what the policeman asked him about, I only heard the shots. Then from the distance I saw Hilmi, Ramush's father. Then after the fire, I didn't see anything else. I saw Ramush with a weapon coming out of the house, but I was afraid lest I was going to be killed, too, as I said, I left the location, went to the meadow --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, thanks. Can you tell the Trial Chamber this, you said that you saw Hilmi and you said that you saw Ramush and that he also had a weapon coming out of the house. Did Hilmi have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Hilmi, no, he didn't have a weapon. He came at the door to talk with the policemen. About this I heard later, actually. I didn't hear that at that moment. After Otovic died, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Otovic had gone to Ramush's house to ask for him, his father came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So it's very important that we know what you saw with your own eyes and what you heard, okay. So we'd like to make a difference. It's important to the Trial Chamber to know the difference between what you saw and what you heard. So let me ask you this, let me ask you this, just wait for the question. Did you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this may well be a premature interjection but may I take the opportunity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You expect that it would be leading of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, may I take the opportunity just gently to remind Mr. Di Fazio to take very great care.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, why not approach the matter in a very systematic way; that is, to first of all find out where the witness was. Could I just put a few questions to him. Witness, I would have a few questions for you. When this all happened, where did you come from? You said you were passing by. You were coming from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you walking? Were you in a car? Were you on a bike? How did you move from Gjakove to the place where you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was on a bike. I was coming home on a bike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were coming home on a bike. Were you on the main road between Gramaqel and Gllogjan when you passed the house, the Haradinajs' house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not hear the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said you heard shots. Were you still on your bike when you heard these shots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I stopped the bike and then I saw what was going on. I heard the shots, and then I dropped the bike, crossed over a fence, and headed towards that meadow. And then the shots became more intensive and firing continued up until 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me take you back. Let me take you back. One second. The first time you heard a shot, were you still on your bike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And can you tell us how far away you at that moment were when you heard this first shot, you still on your bike, from Haradinajs' house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was 50 metres away, less than 50 metres away. I was very close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you said you came off your bike and you turned then. When you left your bike, did you go to the left of the road or did you go to the right of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went in the direction of Baballoq village. There was no other way for me to go other than Baballoq, to go to the road heading towards Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us just by using your arms what kind of -- what side of the road you went. Could you just indicate that with your arms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the left, to go to the Baballoq village. I was walking on the main road between Gramaqel and Gllogjan on the right side. Then, when I left, I headed for the left to go to Baballoq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me stop you there. When you left that road where you were biking, did you go on another road or did you go on the meadows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the meadow. I didn't dare go to the road. I walked across the meadow because, as I said, there were police cars, people started shooting, the situation became very confusing and chaotic, so I didn't dare go to the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you heard this first shot, were there already more than one police car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was one police car, a Golf, belonging to Momo Milic, not the police car but a Golf car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So do I understand then, if you went to the meadows that you moved away -- away from the Haradinajs' house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I left that place. I moved away because I was afraid of being killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how far did you go from the road to the left and to the meadows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went to Baballoq village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Immediately or after a while?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After a while because I didn't dare leave immediately. There was a brook running by and all of us entered, women, children, all of us went to that place and rested there. When evening came, it was about 6.00 or 7.00 p.m., at that time we went to Baballoq village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But when you heard the shot, when you got off your bike, did you immediately go to that brook or did you stay nearby the Haradinaj house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went immediately. I was very close to their house. There was a meadow dividing us, so I saw everything. I saw the army, the car. You could see everything from where we were. There were some trees hiding us from being seen by the police. You could see women, children, they had taken shelter there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment. What you tell us now, that must have been later, isn't it, because you said there was only one police car in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One. There was only one, but after Otovic got killed they called their headquarters and the police and the -- the police and the army came immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. But what I would like to know is how far you went into the meadows immediately after you heard that shot. When you got off your bike, you went into the meadows, so within that one or two minutes, how far away did you move from the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to tell you, not more than 200 metres away because that was a good hiding place at the brook. There we rested a while and then, as I said, in the evening at about 7.00, 7.30 - I couldn't be exact because I didn't look at the time - we entered Baballoq. There we stayed, we spent the night there, and on the next day I went back home and asked about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. When you moved into the meadows, did you look back at the road and the house or did you just run, as you said, the 200 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We ran as fast as we could because shots were being heard from all sides, all sorts of weapons were firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was still immediately after you got off your bike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because in 10, 15 minutes the police and the army came to the village --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I'm talking not about 10, 15 minutes; I'm talking about the first minute you got off your bike.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I heard the shot from Ramush's house, I dropped my bike, as I said, and crossed over a fence heading towards Baballoq walking on a meadow. Near the brook was where I stopped and hid myself, and there were many other people there who were trying to flee the village, women, children. Only the police and the army were left in the village and those KLA, I don't know, who were fighting with the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I'm aware that I took some of your time. We are about to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I -- if at all possible, I prefer the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Because now I can just recap, go through the transcript and see if there's anything else that I want to raise on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And be of some assistance to me. I also understand that we may be able to get an image up and if we have the break now that might enable me to assist with some area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the last few answers, I don't know -- of course, I don't know what else you have in mind, but if there is anything about the house of the witness and the Haradinaj house, then I would like to know where exactly they are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can only promise to do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before we break, immediately before Your Honour began to question the witness, he indicated in answer to Mr. Di Fazio, that when he first heard the shots he was close to Ljubica's house, and I wonder if we might just invite him to confirm by that he means --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not mind at all if it clarifies the issue. It's at least a very concrete matter which I could not immediately from the top of my head give a follow-up, but if that could be done after the break that would be appreciated. Then, Witness, Mr. Jollaj, we'll have a break for 25 minutes. We'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps before I do, I indicate that there's a black-and-white copy of the photograph that was on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- moments before. Yes. You can see it now, that's D35. I'll attempt to, if I may, show the witness that and see how far I can go with that. If he can't recognise it, I intend to move on fairly swiftly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand -- Witness, I'd like you to have a look at a black-and-white aerial photograph. You may also be able to see a colour version of that photograph on the screen down there where you are. Could you have a look at it and tell us if you recognise that place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The place where Ramush's house was? I'm not clear about your question. Can you be more explicit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know which little village or town that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what to say now? Things have changed. I may make some mistakes. It's another view now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise it at all? That's all. If you don't recognise it, just tell us and then we will know what to do. Just tell us, do you recognise that place at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I -- are you asking me about Gllogjan village or about some other village? I don't think that this picture shows Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I intend to move on now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just before the break you mentioned someone whose house you were close to when you -- during the shooting episode. You mentioned a man named Ljubica. Do you have his -- can you tell the Trial Chamber what his surname is, Ljubica's surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ljubica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did he have a couple of sons; and if so, do you know what their names were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragoslav, there was another one who was a policeman, and two others, but they left they -- they left the village. I don't know where his two sons were staying. I know that one of them was a policeman in the Gjakove and I know that there was this Dragoslav, this Dragan, I think there were four or five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already touched upon this, but I want to know on the day that Otovic was shot, the day that you've been talking about, do you know approximately how many Serb policemen were operating -- came to the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, there were many policemen who came, we were hidden. I can't say now. I can't tell you the number of cars. I couldn't say there were two or three or five, but there were many, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And during the day was there fighting going on, shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from 9.00, 9.30, until in 8.00 in the evening when they stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you -- can you tell the Trial Chamber if there were any helicopters present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was. There were three helicopters that I saw and three youths were killed, three Albanian youths, and I knew them, and I felt very sorry for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Were -- was there any firing or shooting from the helicopters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't see that because they flew in the direction of Shaptej, and I don't want to lie here to tell you that they shot or not. I don't know. I can't say something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Following -- thank you. Following this episode that you've told us about this afternoon when Mr. Otovic was shot and the fighting that you've described, what did you and your family do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed in the house. At about 6.00 or 6 and a half in the morning, I asked my family members what happened. I knew that Otovic was killed, but I didn't know anything about those three young people. As I said, I was in the hiding, so my wife and my sons told me that three youths, and they told me the names, were killed at the school of Shaptej.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you remain in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not for long, after the event when Otovic died. I can't give you the exact date, however, but I know that not even a month passed before I left. The KLA started to grow in numbers. One day I saw many of them, and I left them. They beckoned to me. I wasn't wearing any uniforms. My sons didn't wear any uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just, Mr. Jollaj, let's go back and try and deal with this a little more carefully. You've told us about the episode where Mr. Otovic was killed, you've told us about the fighting. Now, now, just think back --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- after that you said you remained in Gllogjan. How long did you stay in Gllogjan after Mr. Otovic was killed would you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's helpful. Now, try and think -- okay. Thank you, that's helpful --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Was it a question of hours or days or weeks that you stayed in Gllogjan after Mr. Otovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three weeks I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Gjakove where my wife was there in hospital for a month and a half. She was in a critical condition. My sons and my father remained there, and the -- my daughter-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Slow it down. That's -- slow it down. Okay. You -- after Mr. Otovic was killed, you said you stayed in Gllogjan for about two or three weeks. Just hear -- listen to me. Okay. Just listen to me. You were there for about two or three weeks, and then you went to Gjakove and your wife was in hospital --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I went to Gjakove --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did -- now, when you went to Gjakove, did you leave some --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- my second son.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. When you went to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed with some in-laws. My wife's father was living there --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and her brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, would you please answer the question, then stop, not tell anything else unless specifically asked for by Mr. Di Fazio. So please give brief answers and do not interrupt Mr. Di Fazio so that he can finish his questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, when you went to Gjakove, did any of your family members remain behind in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my father, my eldest son who was 23/24 years old, my daughter, my daughter-in-law, and their two children. They remained in the village. I had my livestock --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I had other house belongings, a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, you went to Gjakove. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there until the war was over, and then I returned from Albania where I stayed with some acquaintances of mine. My son worked as a private -- in a private company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever go back to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We returned with my wife and my son. We visited the house, worked in the garden, and had my car repaired. I stayed there, I went out, I took walks, and then I took my wife again for a medical check-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Gllogjan when you came back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not remain there. I stayed there for just one night and then went back, because I had to take my wife back there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Take your wife back where exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to take her to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Did you -- after that, did you go back to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only went once back there during the war. My second son also went to that house, but he came back again. We were not working as private operators anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We worked in the villages. We couldn't stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this: After Mr. Otovic was killed, did you ever see Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Otovic was killed, I can't remember, to be honest. I don't think I saw him. Maybe he passed by with the army. I don't know, because Ramush was heading the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Mr. Jollaj, it's not in dispute that you left Gllogjan. We know you left Gllogjan. Now, can you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- just listen to my question and listen carefully, listen carefully, okay? Can you explain, please, to the Judges who are listening to you why you left Gllogjan. Why? Why? What was your reason? Why did you leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left because of my wife's situation. She was in a critical condition. Six people gave blood for her until she got her sight back. I had to go to the hospital with her. And to speak the truth, I also was a little afraid to remain because there were problems in the village. I was afraid that I would be killed or something should happen to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell the Trial Chamber why you were afraid that something might happen to you. What was troubling you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is another reason. I was afraid that -- things were being said in the village. Ramush, Ramush's father said things like I had joined the Serbs, I had worked for the Serbs. It is true that I worked for Serbs privately. I had to work to keep my family, to earn a living. And I didn't pay attention whether the person I worked for was a Serb or an Albanian, a Muslim, or a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell the Trial Chamber from whom you learnt that this was being said about you, from whom? Who said that this -- these words were being spoken about you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were said to me even before the war. I had problems with some young people who said to me, You're keeping company with the Serbs. These were things that had no sense. I was not paying attention to politics --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- or anything else. I just wanted to work and keep my family alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The young people who said these things to you, were they young people from the village or were they young people from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were from my own village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were friends. I could call them friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, think back, did you hear that these things were being said before or after the Serb policeman Otovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This thing -- these things were said even before. They said some words, but I didn't pay attention to them, things like I was keeping company with the Serbs. I was minding my own business trying to work and earn a living for my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I grew up there together with them, in the same village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about after the Serb policeman Otovic was killed, were these things also said to you after he was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, things were mentioned, but these things made no sense to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, you've said that these words had something to do with your leaving Gllogjan and your wife's illness had something to do with leaving Gllogjan. Were those the only reasons you left Gllogjan or are there any other reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was my wife who was ill, but as I said these words were said before. But however, I went about in the villages without any problems before. I spent my whole life in the village. There was no problem with my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do your best and try and tell the Trial Chamber when was the last time you ever saw or laid eyes on Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last time -- well, I cannot give you an exact answer. I don't know. I only remember that when they came out in the beginning, in uniform, they all got together, and that was the time when I learned what the KLA was. Because until then I didn't know anything or I hadn't seen them. So it was at about 10.00 or 12.00 that day when I saw them preparing themselves, preparing the positions, that's when I saw Ramush for the last time. I don't think I saw him later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour give me one moment for an in-court consultation with my client?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour extend that courtesy to me for one further moment to consult with co-counsel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, I would have a few questions for you. You told us that you were very close to Ljubica's house when you heard the shots. Could you tell us whether you had passed Ljubica's house already when you heard them or were you exactly where his house is or were you just approaching where his house is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was approaching. I was close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us how close, another 10 metres? Another 15 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I'm sorry. I'm not sure. There is a field between the two houses and this's the road as well, so I don't know, 50 metres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you said you got off your bike once you heard the shot or shots. Could you tell us whether you got off your bike before you were at a point where Ljubica's house is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had left, or rather, I had gone past Ljubica's house for about 10, 15 metres, and between Ljubica's house and the main road that leads to Gllogjan, that's where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One more question for you. You earlier said that Ramush Haradinaj came out of the house with a gun. Was that after you had heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was when I was approaching Ramush's house. I saw the policemen when they called, and Hilmi, Ramush's father, came out. And immediately after Hilmi, Ramush came out with a gun, and he shot Otovic. This is what I saw. I saw Otovic falling down, and immediately I tried to leave. It was only 50 metres away, so the bullets were there. And as I told you earlier, I ran towards the direction of Baballoq, I stopped at the brook, and I joined the group of people who were trying to leave the village, whole families, children, and women, and so on. And then the army came and there were -- there was shooting everywhere --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time did it take you to get to the brook where you said others were already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were people leaving, they left their houses, all of them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could you please focus on my question, that is: How much time did it take you when you got from your bike to get to where you say -- you said you saw other people, how much time, one minute, three minutes, so crossing the meadow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, really, about ten minutes I would think. I went to that small stream of water and got together with some people, and further on there was the brook. There were many more people there, families, whole families, trying to leave. I helped them to cross the brook, get on the other side, carried their children. So I tried to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did they tell you why they were all there when, as far as I understand, it was only a couple of minutes before that you heard one shot fired and where the other police forces had not yet come to that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People had heard the shots from Ramush's house, and shots were heard from other places in the villages -- in the village from the houses. So whole families left immediately. Children, women were going through the meadows, through the fields. The whole population tried to leave. This happened very soon after the shots, and people were trying to go to Baballoq, to Gramaqel, and other villages. Everybody was trying to get their families out, to take them to Gjakove, wherever they could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I'd like to take you back to a few things you said before, and I'll read slowly to you part of your testimony of today. You said: "It was Hilmi, Ramush's father, whom the policeman asked something -- actually, I didn't hear what the policeman asked him about. I only heard the shots." You then continued: "Then from the distance I saw Hilmi, Ramush's father, then after the fire I didn't see anything else. I saw Ramush with a weapon coming out of the house, but I was afraid lest I was going to be killed too, as I said." Now, this suggests that you saw Ramush Haradinaj coming out of the house after you heard the shots, or is that not correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. When the policemen went there to Ramush's house, and I saw the policemen close to the gate, I saw Hilmi speaking to them. Hilmi went inside and Ramush came out with the gun in his hand and fired, and I saw Otovic falling down. I also recognised the other policeman Momo Milic, and Momo Milic -- because there was some workers working there doing the fence around the house. So Momo Milic took one of these workers and used him as a shield to protect himself and went up to the car like that to get into the car. And he notified the police, and then the police from Irzniq, from Gjakove, and from Peje, from wherever, they all came. The army came, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me stop you again there. I'll read another part of your statement to you -- of your testimony to you. You said: "Hilmi, he didn't have a weapon, he came at the door to talk with the policeman. About this I heard later, actually. I didn't hear that at that moment. After Otovic died, I heard that." What did you exactly hear and from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hilmi did not have a weapon when he came out and spoke to the policemen, he was unarmed. Hilmi went in to call Ramush, for him to come out and speak to the policemen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please again listen to my question. You said that you heard -- you said: "About this I heard later, actually. I didn't hear that at that moment. After Otovic died, I heard that." My question is: What did you hear exactly after Otovic died, and did you hear that from someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Otovic was killed - and I saw him being killed - the houses around started to shoot as well -- people from the houses started to shoot as well. There was no house from where there was no shooting. And at that moment I decided to leave and go to Baballoq. There was no other way for me. How could I stay there? As I already told you, Hilmi was not armed. He went in to call Ramush to come out, and Ramush came out and he was armed and he fired on Otovic. And for 10 or 15 minutes there was shots from all over the village. I don't know how to explain this better to you. Only if you were there yourselves and saw everything with your own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, I have no further questions to you. Have the questions of the Bench raised any issue you would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, they have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jollaj, Mr. Emmerson has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if the registrar could help us, please, by turning to the bundle of documents that are available to the registry in Belgrade and to tab 20, which is an aerial photograph in colour of the area around the Haradinaj compound. I can hand hard copies to the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the aerial photograph 1D020733.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a new aerial photograph, it's a Prosecution document. Can I first check with the registry, please, that that is a colour photograph with a large building in the bottom centre of it. Perhaps the witness could hold the photograph up to the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Belgrade] Yes, that is a photograph. Unfortunately, the photograph has no markings on it, no ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be shown to the camera in Belgrade so that we can verify that we are looking at the same ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I guess I don't -- one second, please. Yes, that's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So can the record please show that the photograph that the witness has is the photograph that we have, and can that please be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be D160, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you could just look, please, at that photograph closely for a moment, please, Mr. Jollaj, you will see a main road running across the photograph horizontally, or rather, diagonally from the top left to halfway down the right-hand side. Perhaps the registrar could just assist in identifying the road we're discussing. So it runs diagonally across the top half of the photograph, from the top left to roughly halfway down to the right-hand side. Do you see that road, Mr. Jollaj? What I'm asking you to do at the moment is to orientate yourself on the photograph. Do you see the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, that is the main road leading -- that is the main road leading from Dubrave on the left --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, the main road here. This is the main road. I understand you. On the right, here, I can't see this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. If you just follow my questions, if you would, for a moment. Can you see a line of trees that runs diagonally up towards the road from the left-hand side of the photograph? Do you see that line of trees that runs from the left side of the photograph up diagonally towards the road, do you see that? Can you just confirm that you identified the line of trees for us, please, Mr. Jollaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This here is a tree-lined part on the right I think, when you go towards Gramaqel and this is the brook, the waterway --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, there seems to be some -- everyone is pointing at a different matter I see on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's see if we can get [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar in Belgrade has pointed at the line of trees I think you have in mind. Madam Registrar, could you please again point to the same line of trees as you did before and everyone can now follow it on the screen. Yes, please, from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So running from the left-hand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could do it in front of the camera as well. You pointed at which line of trees?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the line of trees, yes. Could you please put it again in front of the witness and point that specific line of trees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The trees, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you see just between the road that we've looked at and the line of trees, there is a white mark in a field. Can you see that white mark? And perhaps the registrar could assist you there as well. There's a white circular mark of what looks like a ruined building between the line of trees and the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you again point at that in front of the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please point at that for the witness, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, so that you understand the photograph, Mr. Jollaj, that white mark that you're looking at there is the position where the Stojanovic house used to stand. Do you recognise that, that position, as the position where the Stojanovic house was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, pausing there for a moment, is that where you were when you heard the shots along the road adjacent to that spot there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you look at the large building in the centre of the photograph, that is the Haradinaj family compound. So it's the largest building in the foreground, and don't be misled by it because it's bigger now in this photograph than it was at the time. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Smajl Haradinaj's house maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, the large --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe Ramush's uncle's house. One belongs to Haxhibeka, he's also from Haradinaj family, and one belong's to Smajl Haradinaj's.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you see the large building in the centre of the photograph just below halfway up, there's a large building with a white wall running across the middle of it. Can you see that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the upper half of that building was present in 1998, I suggest, yes, and that was Hilmi Haradinaj's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that was Hilmi Haradinaj's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that we're clear, when you heard the shots, do you say that from where you were you could see where Mr. Otovic was standing at the time that the shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I passed on to the left and left a little -- went away a little from the place where I was standing, and I went to this hiding place. Then I went closer to Baballoq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's very important, Mr. Jollaj, that we separate out what you were told later on by people from what you actually saw at the time. And I'm asking you about the time when you heard the shots. And you've told us at the time when you heard the shots you were on the road adjacent to where the Stojanovics' house is. And I'm asking you: Could you see where it was that Mr. Otovic fell, could you see where he fell? Did you actually see him fall with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see Otovic falling down because I was too scared. I tried to run away as fast as I could because, as I said, I was holding the bicycle and then I had to drop the bicycle. And the police were coming, and I was very close to the place where the event had taken place. It's -- the house is about 50 metres away from the road, so I was scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sure we all understand that you were scared and that maybe you didn't want to look, but what I want to be clear about is you didn't see Mr. Otovic fall with your own eyes. Did you ever see his body in the roadway or did you not see that either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see the actual place where he fell, I didn't, I couldn't see that. I couldn't even look in that direction. I was -- to tell you the truth, I was very scared. I just heard the shot and tried to flee, to save myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us that you thought you saw Ramush with a gun, but can I be clear --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ramush was with a weapon in his hand, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you saw that, did you, from the Stojanovics' house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I passed the house of Stojanovic. It was a canal with water running by, and you -- that water divided Ramush's plot from Stojanovics' house and I saw him when he shot and then I left immediately and didn't see any further than that. I wanted to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sure we understand. But as you walked past you didn't notice where Mr. Otovic was at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I was passing. I wasn't interested in following up what happened. I just wanted to flee. I was -- I wasn't interested at all in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does it come to this, you saw someone you thought was Ramush Haradinaj with a gun, and you heard some shots, and then you ran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I ran.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, just one other matter briefly, if I may, with you on this topic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The -- do you see where the main road crosses or joins, rather -- let me put the question again. Do you see where the main road that we've been discussing that you were on joins the road towards the Haradinajs' house? Do you see that, the intersection on the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if I tell you that Mr. Otovic's body was recorded as having been found on the main road itself, can you help us as to where it was you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not on the main road when he was killed. He was near the gate of Ramush's house 10 or 15 metres away from the door, from the gate, at least it's approximately that distance. I didn't measure it. After what happened, I told you I didn't look in that direction anymore. I don't know what happened after that. I only know that there was a lot of shooting going on. I just wanted to flee as fast as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, you drew a plan of this incident when you were interviewed by the Prosecution in August 2002, and you marked a place where you said Otovic was killed as being on the main road. Is it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did the drawing myself and I can draw it even today, but it is not a main road. The main road that goes to Gllogjan from Irzniq -- from Irzniq to Gllogjan, and from Gllogjan to Gramaqel, this road -- there is a deviation in -- from this road in the direction of Ramush's house, and it's rather long stretch of road. But he was not killed on the main road that goes directly to Gramaqel, but in that stretch of road that goes in the direction of Ramush's house. I did the drawing myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we obviously have a record of the statement that you made and the drawing that you did, and I'm not going to try to go through the pictures with you now, but I'm suggesting to you, Mr. Jollaj, what you drew in 2002 was a marking in which you said that Mr. Otovic had died on that road, the main road, opposite the entrance to the Haradinaj home, which is indeed where he is recorded as having been found on the police report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe -- I didn't draw it very well because I am not a professor of drawing. It is an approximate drawing. I am an illiterate man. Just to give you an idea of what happened, to help you, this is why I did it, but he was not killed on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you saw the man that you thought was Ramush Haradinaj with a gun, were you still at the Stojanovics' house at that time, or rather, adjacent to the Stojanovics' house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not at his house but very close to his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If I give you an indication that there's a distance of approximately 175 metres from the position of the Stojanovic property to the position of the Haradinaj property, does that help you at all as to how far away you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left Stojanovics' house. I showed you before. As to how many metres the distance is from Ramush's house or even Ljubica's house from Ramush's, I couldn't give you an accurate figure. Maybe 350 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 150 or so, I can't tell for sure, even closer maybe, Ramush's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Jollaj, on this photograph, looking at the picture again, where was it that you fled into the fields towards the brook? Looking at the photograph, either describe it to us or mark it on the picture if you -- if that's easier. Which was the direction you took to flee across the fields and into the brook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I showed you. I left on the left. If you come from Gramaqel to enter Gllogjan, I left on -- in the left direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you look at the photograph, please, and identify for us, perhaps mark it with a pen, where it was you turned off the road towards the brook.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you ask me how many metres I was away from Ramush's house and Stojanovics' house, I couldn't be very accurate. I don't want to lie to you. I was in between Stojanovics' and Haradinajs' house. That is where I was, and when I was there I took the left direction if you come from Baballoq village --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, towards Baballoq village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Jollaj, I've just got a have you few questions. Defence counsel have said to you that you were adjacent to the Stojanovics' house. Thinking back, can you try and tell the Trial Chamber a little more accurately how close you were to the Stojanovic's house when you saw these events. Were you right next to it, close to it, or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had just passed that house and some coming near Ramush's house. Stojanovics' house is further down where I was. There is a brook or a waterway there that flows in the middle of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's used for irrigation, you know, so it's kind of guiding line between Stojanovic and Haradinajs' house, I was in the middle of these two houses. And then I took the left direction in the direction of Baballoq. And then, as I said, we rested for a while in that place with the other families and then we left that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
