utterances.text: And just one last question. Okay. You've told us that you were between the two houses in the middle of these two houses. Can you tell the Trial Chamber if you had walked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, I was in between the two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the Stojanovic house --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Wait for the question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and the Haradinajs' house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just wait for it and then you'll know what the question is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's all right. Just wait for it. You said you were between the Stojanovic -- and just wait for it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's between.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, can you tell us, can you tell the Trial Chamber if -- where you were in relation to that line of trees that you can see in the photograph. Had you gone past the line of trees or were you before it when you saw the events concerning Mr. Otovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was -- there were some lines here like fences. There were some trees a little bit further away. It was a fence there. There wasn't any road. A little bit further there were the trees, but now the layout has changed. It's not like it was before. There were fences, there were trees, now I don't see -- hedges, so it's difficult for me now to figure out exactly where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you saw the events involving whatever it was that you saw involving Mr. Otovic, were there trees between you and Mr. Otovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were trees in front of Ramush's house, it's a kind of triangle. It's a main tree -- the main road, then it's triangle land, then the road. Here is Ramush's uncle and here is Ramush's house, and that is this place with trees and fence that surrounds that area, that land.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did trees block your view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you couldn't see very well. They prevented me from looking properly. There was a fence, as I said, and the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions, then, Mr. Jollaj, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming to where you are now and to answer all the questions that have been put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I hope that you'll be soon home again, safe with your family.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you what I know; what is not true, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I saw with my own eyes, and I know I told you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for -- thank you for that, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Jollaj. We will have a break now and after the break we'll continue with videolink with the next witness. We'll have a break until ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who's going to deal with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I will be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Ms. Gustafson, I'd like to do the same as before, turn into closed session, we are already, as a matter of fact -- or are we not, Mr. Registrar? We are in open session, although on my screen it says private or closed session. We first then before we go into the videolink we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber has decided to grant protective measures in respect of Witness 65, that is face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym, the reasons to follow. We need a 15-minutes' adjournment in order to prepare for the voice distortion. We resume at 25 minutes to 7.00. --- Break taken at 6.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 65, you'll now be examined first by Ms. Gustafson. Ms. Gustafson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we go into private session to identify the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness 65, just for you to know, we are in open session; that is, the content of your testimony can be heard but your face still cannot be seen. We are not using your name, and your voice cannot be heard. So please keep in mind if you are referring to family members that you talk about my brother or my cousin or my village without mentioning names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not even the village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not even the village. If you say "my village," we know what village it is. Please proceed, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness 65, what was your occupation in 1998 when you were living in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. What did you do for a living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Profession? I worked privately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Private odd jobs here and there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So did you work for other families in the village and around the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked for my own family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you also work for other families in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Other families? I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: For example, did you do odd jobs for other people, other people that weren't in your family? Did you work on other people's land?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And what were the ethnicities of the people that you worked for, the people that you did jobs for, and the people whose land you worked on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Albanians, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We lived together, side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that the same for your father and your brother, did they also do the same type of work as you for the same -- different families?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, did you and your family leave your village sometime in 1998? Did you move from your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did. We left the village, all of us, my brother, father, and -- all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We -- when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when was that? When did you and your family leave your village? If you can't remember the date, just remember as best you can the month or the season.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was spring-time when it was the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the day that you left your village, what time of day was it when you left? Was it morning? Noon? Afternoon? Evening? Night-time? What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was around 1.00 or 2.00. To tell you the truth, we didn't -- it didn't even occur to us to look at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you mean 1.00 or 2.00 in the afternoon or 1.00 or 2.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And on that day that you left your village at 1.00 or 2.00 in the afternoon, did anything happen in your village on that morning before you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did, it did. Some Albanians came there. They told my father, Where are your sons? Why aren't you asking your sons to wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, is this something you saw and heard yourself or is this something your father told you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father told me. I wasn't there. I was working because I had to win the bread of my -- for my family. And then we left the village. We went to another village, to another place not far from the actual village one or two hours away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And when your father told you that some Albanians came and asked him why his sons weren't wearing uniforms, did he tell you what kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To wear Albanian uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Uniforms of some force, some organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the KLA. They didn't have uniforms. They were civilians, those who came to our house. This is what my father told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, there's some confusion about who was wearing uniforms and the question about not wearing uniforms. Perhaps we could clarify that. Your father told you that those who came asked why his sons were not wearing uniforms. What kind of uniforms did they expect the sons of your father to wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said, Why don't you ask your sons to join?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To join what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To join them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who are "them"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Albanians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but any specific -- any specific force? I mean if you say, Why don't you join them, that's -- join who exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Albanians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father told them, I cannot ask my sons to join because otherwise I will be left only with two girls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you said to join the Albanians. Did you, since they were talking about uniforms, did your father understand this as far as he told you that you should join an armed -- an Albanian armed force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know any name of such an armed force or did your father tell you about any name of such an armed force which you were suggested to join?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were from Gllogjan. They -- he didn't know them. He said they are from Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked whether the armed force -- you were -- it was suggested that you would join and wear uniforms, uniforms of what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The liberation army of Albanians, the KLA for short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, just so that I'm clear and perhaps I misunderstood something. As I understood this gentleman's testimony on line 5, the people who came were not wearing uniforms and they were civilians I'm just trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm just trying to -- because the word "they" was used a couple of times, and I thought that I might be -- kind of be confused that the individuals who were having this discussion with his father were civilians. I just wanted to make sure that I -- that I hadn't misread the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Ms. Gustafson wants to give this a follow-up then of course it's up to her.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm happy with the answers. I'll just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At this point when your father told you about this conversation, did you belong to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we left, we left the village. We left the house immediately, on the same day, my brother, my mother, the children, my sisters were married.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. And before the time that you left your village, had you ever belonged to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about your brother, had he ever belonged to the KLA before that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about your cousin, did he ever belong to the KLA before that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, none of us belonged to the KLA. We didn't side with anyone. We simply worked for our daily bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we move into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You said they came and took your brother. Do you remember the date on which your brother was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The 4th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. My father told me the date. They took him, I don't know where to. I looked for him high and low, but I couldn't find him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was the 4th of July. What time of day was it when they came and took your brother? Was it morning? Afternoon? Evening? What time of day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was before -- around 12.00 or before 12.00, before midday. I didn't have a watch. I was in the yard, and I had a fruit in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were in the yard, it was 12.00, around midday. Was your brother in the yard with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother was in the street. It was on a higher place. They took him. We were eating and they came and asked me about my cousin, asking me where he was, and I retorted I didn't know, and then they beat me --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and when they beat me -- can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I know this is difficult, but I'd really like you to just answer my questions one at a time and wait for my next question before you answer and make your questions as brief and direct -- make your answers as brief and direct as possible. All right? Now, you said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. We can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I asked you if your brother was in the yard and you said yes, and then you said my brother was in the street. Where was your brother when the people came and took him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There, (redacted), near me. He went out in the street. I was eating with other members. He went out --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I apologise. He went to a shop to get some cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you said your brother had gone out into the street. Did he come back to the yard where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. They took him away when he was outside, in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went out and said to them, Don't take away my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So was this in the street immediately outside the yard that you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't very far from where I was. When I went out I told them not to take my brother away. They put him in a car and then they came back to the yard where I was and they start -- gave me a good beating and they pushed my wife and swore at her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see the people approach who came and took your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I saw them and I remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they approach in vehicles or on foot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They left the vehicles in the street, and they were there with my brother. Then they came to where I was. When they beat me, I got up on my feet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How many vehicles and how many people came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know all of them, I didn't count them, but I know there were many of them, some seven or eight cars I would say. One was wearing black clothes, a black hood on his face. He asked me, (redacted) And I answered, I don't know -- I said I don't know him -- in fact, I didn't say I didn't know him, but I said I don't know where he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This is as good a time as any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I just said it's as good a time as any to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 65, we will adjourn for the day. It's 7.00. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. We'd like to see you back then. And I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony you have given until now and the testimony you're still about to give tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We stand adjourned. Mr. Registrar, what courtroom are we in tomorrow, are we in III or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, Courtroom III, that's the 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 25
